subject: Request: Shorter tenant telemetry retention + evidence pack
messages:
From: Jason Park <jason.park@orchardtech.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orchardtech.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Shorter tenant telemetry retention request (OrchardTech)

Hi Stephanie,

We’re working through our vendor data minimization policy and would like Redwood to retain tenant-scoped telemetry (inference traces, ephemeral debug logs, and aggregated perf traces) for 14 days rather than your default 90-day window.

Can you confirm: 1) whether Redwood supports a per-tenant shorter retention window, 2) what artifacts / evidence you can provide (SIG/C A I Q sections, sample deletion certificates, proof-of-delete workflow), and 3) any operational constraints (e.g., impact to incident forensics or SLA-backed retention)?

We’re preparing this as part of our procurement sign-off and will need an evidence package to satisfy our security team. I’ve attached a 1-page infra diagram (orchardtech-sysdiagram.pdf) and a CSV with the tenant IDs we’re discussing.

Thanks,
Jason Park
Head of InfoSec
OrchardTech
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Jason Park <jason.park@orchardtech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Shorter tenant telemetry retention request (OrchardTech)

Jason — thanks for the clear ask and the diagram. Short answer: yes, we can accommodate a 14-day tenant-scoped telemetry TTL for non-forensic telemetry with a small operational caveat. Below is a concise summary and an evidence plan; I’ll loop in Ben and Irene for the compliance & infra impact details.

Summary
- Capability: Redwood’s Private and Dedicated deployments support tenant-scoped retention TTLs; Hosted customers can opt into a tenant-level override for session & debug telemetry.
- Impact: Shortening TTL to 14 days will reduce the window for root-cause investigations. For production incidents where longer trace retention is required, we provide a hold/forensic snapshot process (manual request) that preserves a narrow set of artifacts for up to 180 days on a case-by-case basis.
- Controls: We’ll apply logical deletion and cryptographic keys rotation so retained artifacts become irrecoverable after TTL expiration.

Requested evidence pack (we will produce the artifacts below):
1) SIG/CAIQ mapping excerpt for logging & retention controls (sections: LOG-01, LOG-03, RET-02).
2) A sample proof-of-delete record and deletion job audit (exportable JSON audit line items).
3) A short runbook for the temporary forensic snapshot process and who is authorized to request it.
4) Operational caveat note describing the impact to incident SLA and recommended compensating controls (e.g., alert forwarding during the 14-day window).

Next steps
- I’ll send the SIG excerpts and the sample proof-of-delete in a single ZIP (redwood-sig-evidence.zip) by end of day tomorrow.
- Ben: can you confirm whether customer-provided tenant IDs in the attached CSV will require any cross-tenant mapping on your side for the retention job?
- Irene: can you confirm whether this change requires an internal compliance approval (SOC 2 control exceptions)?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Jason Park <jason.park@orchardtech.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Shorter tenant telemetry retention request (OrchardTech)

FW: internal note -> Jason, thanks for the CSV. I verified the tenant IDs and the mapping is straightforward — no cross-tenant mashups needed. Implementation notes:
- Retention job: We’ll create a per-tenant TTL policy scoped to the telemetry tables you listed; retention enforcement runs as an asynchronous batch job every 6 hours.
- Proof-of-delete: Each enforcement run emits an audit event with hash of deleted objects + timestamp; we can export a signed proof bundle on request.
- Forensics: If you anticipate needing evidence beyond 14 days for a specific legal or regulatory need, we can enable a temporary snapshot preserve (requires written request from the security contact) — that snapshot is scoped and logged.

Attaching: orchard-retention-request.csv (the file you sent) and attaching a sample proof-of-delete export in the evidence ZIP we’ll share.

Ben Carter
Senior Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Jason Park <jason.park@orchardtech.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: security@orchardtech.com, procurement@orchardtech.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Shorter tenant telemetry retention request (OrchardTech)

Thanks Stephanie / Ben — this looks reasonable and addresses our requirements. A couple quick clarifications before procurement signs off:
1) Can the SIG/CAIQ excerpt be redacted for internal implementation details but keep the control statements and objective evidence pointers?
2) Please confirm the signed proof-of-delete format (we need a verifiable hash + time + Redwood signer).

If those two items are fine, procurement will proceed with the PO and we’ll include the forensic snapshot SLA in our contract addendum.

We look forward to the evidence ZIP.

—Jason
Head of InfoSec, OrchardTech
